Discipline Priest Rotation in 

Healing, in general, has less of a strict rotation and more of a priority list. Everything that Discipline does in PvE flows through Atonement . In dungeons, you primarily use Power Word: Radiance to apply it with Power Word: Shield s weaved in as well. During raids, you use Power Word: Shield , Plea , and Flash Heal to apply Atonement to 5 allies, followed by using Evangelism to apply 5 more Atonement s, then using both charges of Power Word: Radiance to cover the final 10 players for a total of 20. Discipline tends to follow 3 key rules:

 

 
 Always be casting: Ensure that you are always maintaining Shadow Word: Pain and casting Penance and Smite during downtime to make the most of your Atonement buffs. These smaller heals during downtime really add up over the course of an encounter! 

 

 

 
 Discipline is a "Ramping" Healer: Discipline Priests thrive in a raid environment where they are covering specific and consistent damage events that they can prepare for. Sites like Lorrgs are amazing when preparing for raid encounters so you can observe trends where other players used their cooldowns to burst for the most healing. Knowing what mechanics require "ramping" up your Atonement count to then unleash a flurry of damage abilities is absolutely imperative to your success. Furthermore, Discipline does not heal in steady quantities. A common mistake for new Discipline players is trying to always maintain atonements forever. Instead, you should be aware of when damage goes out and its duration, set up a large quantity of Atonements before hand, and then follow up with damage until many of your Atonements are expiring, then watch your timers for the next round of damage before setting up more atonements. 

 

 

 
 Mythic+ Healing can be polarizing: Discipline is at its strongest with cooldowns like Evangelism or your Voidweaver Rift. While in a raid group, you can count on other Healers to compensate for periods of lower healing from you while you are in your cooldown period. In dungeons, however, you need to be prepared to compensate for when you are lacking a cooldown all on your own. That means that smart usage of the revamped Archangel , which brings a flat heal and absorption increase, or your damage reduction in Pain Suppression is key to mitigating damage on your allies when you are not as easily able to heal them up. Ultimate Penitence is also a powerful cooldown that also doubles as a large defensive so try to find times to cast this when you and your team are taking heavy damage. 
 

Discipline Priest Starter Guide

 Best Discipline PriestRotation

 Stop your Camera moving during Penance
 

This input is a one-time console command that you can paste and enter into your chat box and will stop your camera from moving all over the place when you are Penancing an ally. Note that your character will still turn!
/console cameraSmoothTrackingStyle 0

 Key Macros 

These Smite and Penance macros allow you to spam each spell even when Penance is channeling and it will not "clip" or interrupt the Penance channel, allowing you to guarantee that all bolts are launched before you begin your next cast. 
#showtooltip Smite
/cast Smite

#showtooltip Penance
/cast Penance

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Discipline Priest: Raid, Oracle Mythic+ and Voidweaver Mythic+.

 
 Best Discipline Priest Raid Rotation

 Discipline's ramp profile has been made significantly with the update to Evangelism causing it to cast a Power Word: Radiance and make your next two Power Word: Radiance casts instant. This greatly accelerates your timeline to set up your Atonement s before damage goes out, making it about ~8 seconds instead of the ~15 seconds of set up that it was before. Ultimate Penitence is a very competitive healing cooldown that you would use separately from your Evangelism use.
 
Ramp Timeline

 Core fundamentals 
 
Maintain Shadow Word: Pain on your enemies if the duration is less than 20 seconds.

Cast Void Shield any time it is available.

Use Penance defensively.

Cast Power Word: Shield for your ramp listed above and on cd if mana is in good shape (fights with lots of execute value you'll be able to cast more Shields).

Use Plea and Surge of Light / Flash Heal s to cheaply apply Atonement .

Use Evangelism on cd, just before high damage periods to apply 5 atonements.

Cast Power Word: Radiance s back to back, preferring one cast on melee and one on ranged if allies are spread out.

Cast Shadow Word: Death IF in execute (sub 20%) OR if your Mindbender / Shadowfiend is active this triggers Inescapable Torment value which is very high damage.

Use Penance defensively to heal an injured ally, do not overcap!

Cast Mind Blast on cd, this will empower your next Penance with Dark Indulgence .

Spam Smite during downtime.

Cast Power Word: Shield with Weal and Woe stacks freely if mana is plentiful, fights with more execute value will allow you to cast shields more aggressively.
 

 Mini-Ramps will feature 1-2 Power Word: Radiance casts alongside cheaper atonement applicators like Surge/FHs, Pleas and defensive Penances with shields weaved in if mana is plentiful.

Sniping executes, aka casting Shadow Word: Death on enemies sub 20% is one of the most important things you can be doing as Discipline in raids to improve your performance. Spawning a Shadowfiend will regen mana and contribute to a significant amount of additional Atonement application. That extra mana can funnel into more Atonement application, especially buffed up Power Word: Shield casts through Weal and Woe and result in a ton of extra output. Every time that adds are out, look to snipe an execute on a target. With the 12.05 changes you are no longer running Expiation so you do not need to worry about DoTing the target in advance.

 
Oracle Mythic+ Healing

 Discipline is moving to a shield-centric build in 12.05 and away from a pet-focus, as a result your mana regen is going to be significantly weaker but your shields will be extremely powerful. Look to always drink and have mage food at the ready. You can use Power Word: Shield frequently but keep in mind the mana cost and reduce your casts of normal shields (still using Void Shield constantly!) if your mana is in a poor position. Ultimate Penitence should be used separately from Evangelism in most cases to be as efficient as possible with your healing cooldowns.
 
Standard Oracle Healing Setup

 
Priority

 
Maintain/Spread Shadow Word: Pain . It is much stronger in Midnight, so you will want to make sure you are using Penance offensively (to spread Pain) on trash pulls and defensively on single-target boss fights .

Cast Void Shield any time it is available.

Watch for Shadow Mend procs and weave them in as needed for high spot-healing.

Use Evangelism to apply Atonement s to allies, Power Word: Radiance if you need to refresh on everyone or defensive Penance to refresh indivdual atonements and heal.

Cast Shadow Word: Death on sub 20% hp targets or if you need a damage global on the move.

Cast Penance defensively on allies if you do not need to spread Pain or all enemies already have Pain on them.

Cast Mind Blast 

Cast Penance defensively on allies

Spam Smite and use Penance on cooldown.

Use Power Word: Shield s as needed to supplement. Constant use can OOM you!
 

 
Standard Voidweaver Healing Setup

 
Voidweaver Priority

 
Maintain/refresh Shadow Word: Pain . It is much stronger in Midnight so you will want to make sure you are applying at least one and then letting Penance spread the DoT.

Cast Void Shield any time it is available.

Use Evangelism (or Power Word: Radiance if Evang is on cd) to apply Atonement s to allies.

Cast Shadow Word: Death always on cooldown, even if the target is out of execute range, this triggers Expiation value which is very high damage.

Cast Mind Blast 

Cast Penance offensively

Cast Shadow Word: Death always on cooldown, even if the target is out of execute range.

Spam Void Blast and use Penance on cooldown.

Use Power Word: Shield on cooldown during downtime.
 

 Discipline Priest Major Cooldown Usage

There are many small intricacies to Atonement interactions that can be confusing. Here is a quick list of interactions that demonstrate how Atonement functions.

 
Damaging trinkets and "non-Priest" damage does not convert into Atonement healing.

AoE abilities like Inescapable Torment and Holy Nova only convert into Atonement on one enemy struck.

Reduced or increased damage taken modifiers from outside the Priest do not affect Atonement healing. If the boss has an aura that makes them take 100% more damage, this does not affect Atonement , if the boss takes 99% less damage, that also does not affect Atonement , if the boss is IMMUNE then you will produce ZERO Atonement healing.
 

One of the most challenging concepts for Discipline Priests is timing when to begin your Atonement application. There are two main ways to learn, and most of the time you'll have to do some trial and error to get it just right. 

With a great deal of encounters, you can focus on your Boss Mod of choice to track when an ability hits. With each encounter it can be a bit different, while you may want to ramp for the "Omega Buster" mechanic on the boss mod, that timer may track when the boss begins to cast the ability, not when the damage occurs. So, when first jumping into an encounter, you might end up ramping too early and lose some Atonement s when the boss' cast actually completes. Using a notepad tool on another monitor, using Method Raid Tools or a similar Note addon in game can also help so that you can notate that this "Omega Buster" mechanic has a 5 second cast before it goes out so you'll begin your ramp around 1-2 seconds on the boss mod timer since it'll take around 6 seconds to complete your Atonement application before you can begin damaging to heal. Once you get that first ramp down, you'll generally be able to ramp on cooldown or at the same points on the boss mod timer as before. You can also emphasize and deemphasize boss mechanics to reduce bloat and help you properly visualize when boss mechanics are going to occur to allow you to be more focused.

" Landmark " timing is a method I like to use when raid damage is activated by your raid group. Examples of this would be fights like BNexus King Salhaadar, who spawns Orbs that when killed will deal heavy raid damage. There are boss mod timers for these mechanics but your raid is responsible for killing them and damage can always vary. As a result, I like to use "Landmarks" in the encounter to help me time when I will be ramping. Setting notes so you can track your progress, being aware that you will need to use some trial and error to perfect this will be extremely important.

A couple of things to be aware of with Halo:

OTOH, it's also useful in the open world clusterf*cks of the Faction Assaults. It lets you tag all the mobs in an area, including the bosses that are almost kaput, then when someone else gets the kill, you get the credit.

This is the same reason I run around in those types of fights, dropping Shadow Word: Pain on any and all mobs, to help the players of my faction and get easy kill credit for tagging things. :)

People complain about Discipline Priests not being a good class to play. If that's so, then why do I score the top DPS and HPS on World Boss fights, consistently? :)

It maintains a WoW addon called the Wowhead Looter , which collects data as you play the game! 

 

It uploads the collected data to Wowhead in order to keep the database up-to-date! 

 

 
You can also use it to keep track of your completed quests, recipes, mounts, companion pets, and titles!
